chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), regarding the one in Ihram who dies.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is washed, and enshrouded, and his face is covered, and he is not embalmed, and no perfume touches him.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِِمِ: The one in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.يُحَنَّطُ: He is embalmed (anointed with camphor and spices)
key_terms.يُكَفَّنُ: He is enshrouded (wrapped in burial cloths)

ai.seo_question: What are the funeral rites for a Muslim who dies in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the state of Ihram does not invalidate standard funeral rites, as the deceased is washed and shrouded but specifically exempted from embalming (tadfin) and the application of perfume to the body. This ruling highlights the unique status of the pilgrim, preserving the simplicity of their consecration even in death, a view supported by the majority of Shia jurists who distinguish Ihram from the state of Janabah. The prohibition of perfume underscores the continuity of the ritual state, ensuring the deceased remains in the condition of worship they held at the moment of passing.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Ibn Abu Hamza, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassanasws regarding the one in Ihraam dying.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be washed, and enshrouded, and his face would be covered. Neither would he be embalmed nor touched by anything from the perfumes’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who in the state of Ihram dies.

He (the Imam) said, ‘He is given Ghusl (bath), shroud and his face is covered, but Hunut (rubbing camphor over the seven parts of the body which one places on the ground for Sajdah (prostration)) is not used for him, nor any other kinds of perfumes.”’
